ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60 cm. It is brown with dark, walnut-shaped dorsal blotches and a distinct V-shaped head mark. It features a specialized, blade-like tooth for feeding on reptile eggs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Oligodon juglandifer* is the presence of a distinct, V-shaped dark marking on the nape, which is absent in similar sympatric species.
ai.habitat: The Walnut Kukri Snake inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests and hilly terrain in the eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Walnut Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into reptile eggs, allowing it to feed on the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon juglandifer* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, it likely breeds during the pre-monsoon or monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Walnut Kukri Snake is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
